policy: Neutral wording; claims assessed, not people. Exact quotes only where wording verified from transcript.

claims.claim: "I'll sort of delay caffeine by a little while, usually 90 minutes to two hours."
claims.wording_status: verified quote — Huberman Lab, 'Dr. Matt Walker: The Science & Practice of Perfecting Your Sleep', chapter 'Caffeine' starting 00:49:20

research.text: A 2024 evidence review found no basis in cortisol or adenosine physiology for the claim that delaying morning caffeine prevents an afternoon crash.

claims.reasoning: Mechanism proposed is not demonstrated; no trial tests the delay.

claims.claim: "The subjects also experienced a 250% increase in dopamine concentrations, which, while not 530% as it was with norepinephrine, is still a very large increase in baseline levels of dopamine."
claims.wording_status: verified quote — Huberman Lab, 'Using Deliberate Cold Exposure for Health and Performance' (2022), chapter 'Cold Exposure for Dopamine, Mood & Focus' starting 01:00:22

research.text: Šrámek et al. (n=10) measured ~250% plasma dopamine rise after 1 h immersion at 14 °C; plasma dopamine does not cross the blood–brain barrier.

claims.reasoning: The figure matches the study, but it was plasma dopamine after 1 h at 14 °C; applying it to brain dopamine, mood or brief plunges is untested.

claims.claim: Cold-induced dopamine increase is comparable to cocaine.
claims.wording_status: paraphrase, unverified wording

research.text: The comparison links a human plasma study to a 1989 rat brain microdialysis study; measures are not comparable.

claims.reasoning: Cross-species, cross-compartment comparison.

claims.claim: "If your main goal is hypertrophy and strength, it is probably best to avoid cold-water immersion and ice-bath immersion in the four hours immediately following that strength and/or hypertrophy training."
claims.wording_status: verified quote — Huberman Lab cold-exposure episode, chapter 'Cold, Physical Performance, Inflammation' starting 01:36:22

research.text: An RCT found post-exercise cold water immersion attenuated long-term gains in muscle mass and strength and acute anabolic signalling.

claims.reasoning: Direct RCT evidence.

claims.claim: "Aim for at least 10-15 minutes of sunlight right after waking, especially if you're waking before sunrise."
claims.wording_status: verified wording — written protocol text on the Huberman Lab episode page (Matt Walker episode); not a spoken quote, no timestamp

research.text: Bright light pulses shift human circadian phase in a time-dependent manner (phase response curve).
Transition to bright light in the morning acutely raises cortisol.

claims.reasoning: Core circadian physiology; specific durations recommended are extrapolations.

claims.claim: Evening light from screens delays sleep and circadian timing.
claims.wording_status: paraphrase, unverified wording

research.text: Reading on light-emitting eReaders before bed delayed melatonin and sleep onset vs printed books.

claims.reasoning: Small RCT; effect sizes modest.

claims.claim: "There certainly is a place for blue blockers in the evening and nighttime if you're having issues with falling and staying asleep."
claims.wording_status: verified quote — Huberman Lab, 'Using Light...' episode, chapter 'Tools: Sunlight (UVB), Blue-Light Blockers, Seasonal Affective Disorder' starting 01:12:48

research.text: Cochrane review: blue-light filtering spectacle lenses may not reduce visual fatigue; effects on sleep quality are uncertain (low-certainty evidence).

claims.reasoning: Cochrane finds sleep effects of blue-filtering lenses uncertain; a conditional, evening-only suggestion goes beyond the evidence but isn't contradicted.

claims.claim: There is no safe level of alcohol consumption for health.
claims.wording_status: paraphrase, unverified wording

research.text: WHO Europe states no level of alcohol consumption is safe for health.
GBD 2016 modelling concluded the level minimising health loss is zero.

claims.claim: "Men who used the sauna roughly twice as often, about four to seven times per week, experienced roughly twice the benefits – and were 50 percent less likely to die from cardiovascular-related causes."
claims.wording_status: verified wording — written text on FoundMyFitness sauna topic page (not a podcast quote)

research.text: KIHD cohort (2,315 men, median 20.7 y): HR for sudden cardiac death 0.37 (95% CI 0.18–0.75) for 4–7 vs 1 session/week; similar trend for all-cause mortality.
In the same cohort, adjusted HR for sudden cardiac death was 0.37 (95% CI 0.18–0.75) for 4–7 vs 1 session/week; the paper is observational and a published letter raised self-selection bias.

claims.reasoning: Accurate as an association; causation unproven (observational).

claims.claim: Sauna use extends healthspan / is causally protective.

claims.claim: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA) supplementation reduces cardiovascular risk and supports longevity.
claims.wording_status: paraphrase, unverified wording

research.text: VITAL found no significant reduction in major CV events with 1 g/day omega-3 in a general population.
REDUCE-IT found high-dose icosapent ethyl reduced events in high-risk patients with elevated triglycerides.
Cochrane: little or no effect on all-cause mortality; small reductions in some CHD outcomes.

claims.reasoning: Benefit is population- and dose-specific.

claims.claim: Many people are vitamin D deficient and supplementation has broad health benefits.

research.text: VITAL found vitamin D3 2000 IU/day did not lower invasive cancer or major CV events.

claims.reasoning: Correcting deficiency is reasonable; broad benefits in replete adults not shown.

claims.claim: "Sulforaphane is one that I really like because there's just evidence that sulforaphane is a very powerful activator of the Nrf2 pathway."

research.text: Human trials show biomarker effects (e.g. detoxification of airborne pollutants) but limited hard-outcome data.

claims.reasoning: Nrf2 activation is a well-established mechanism with human biomarker evidence; disease-prevention outcomes remain unproven and should not be inferred from this quote.

claims.claim: VO2max/cardiorespiratory fitness is among the strongest predictors of mortality; low vs elite fitness is ~5× mortality difference.

research.text: A 2025 narrative review argues that popular endorsement of Zone 2 as optimal stems largely from observational data on elite endurance athletes, and that it contradicts substantial evidence supporting high-intensity exercise for improving mitochondrial capacity and cardiometabolic health in the general public.

claims.reasoning: Zone 2 training improves fitness, but evidence that it is superior to higher intensities for the general public is lacking.

claims.claim: "The mice that we've given resveratrol every second day on a normal diet live dramatically longer than any other group."

research.text: Sinclair's group's published study showed resveratrol increased survival of mice on a high-calorie diet.
The NIA Interventions Testing Program found resveratrol had no significant effect on lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice.

claims.reasoning: No published normal-diet lifespan extension was located, and the multi-site NIA test was null. The claim may refer to unpublished data.
